analysis:
Reviewed unit 0 and independently checked the replayed patches. In provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Engine/Bridge/NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.swift:18,224-227 (head), the PR adds bodyTooLarge and replaces the fixed 8 MiB body ceiling with NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes. Positive sizes, the 1 MiB template ceiling and proportional memory quoting remain. docs/reference/nemotron-super-image-formats.md:94 (head) describes a 40 MiB ceiling and media_too_large refusal. At that documented ceiling, the existing formula quotes up to 1300 MiB; this expands admission but does not independently demonstrate an allocation or accounting bypass.

No concrete security regression is supported by the visible changes. They do not directly change encryption, authorization, attestation, credential custody, billing, cache isolation or plaintext storage. Relevant availability and media-memory contracts include TB-007, T-010, T-028 and T-050; no change to T-041's cache mitigations is visible.

Material integration questions remain: verify the actual ServingPolicy constant, encodedHeaderQuote callers and reservation enforcement before JSON/base64/native processing; confirm release on refusal/cancellation and propagation of bodyTooLarge to media_too_large. Also verify the lower HTTP upload cap described in the prior analysis against LocalChatUploadResponder.swift/NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift. Those implementations are not supplied, so neither enforcement nor a missing control can be established. Replay is incomplete (4 of 8 previously reviewed units omitted), including the direct-mode documentation cited by the prior analysis; its claims are not independently validated here. Further review should resolve these expanded-ingress admission and error-handling contracts.
